correction.text: Chang'an and the Wei valley, carried back to 351-352

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the state begins 4 March 351 ("Established: 4 March 351"; Fu Jiàn took Chang'an and claimed the title of Heavenly King of Qin) but Cliopatria starts in 353. The 353 shape (Shaanxi 83 %, Ningxia 73 % of the cells) is carried back two years as a bridge.

388,302 km2 for 353-370: the Guanzhong core round Chang'an. The page describes no territory before the conquest of Yan in 370, so the extent is unverified (page budget); it gives no area figure at all, in the infobox or the text. (unverified: page budget)

1,160,710 km2 for 371-372: Former Yan's realm (Hebei, Shandong, Beijing, Liaoning, Ye, Luoyang) added; "by the end of 370, all of Yan was conquered" and "Chouchi was conquered" in 371, so the shape agrees with the page one year after the event. No infobox area to compare.

1,492,488 km2 for 373-377: Sichuan added (57 % of the province's cells), matching "in 373, they captured Sichuan from Jin". Former Liang and Dai fell in 376; the shape does not yet hold Hexi or Hohhot (the ledger carries 376).

1,798,334 km2 for 378-382, the maximum: Hexi to Dunhuang and Ningxia added after "Qin's unification of northern China was completed in 376" (Former Liang and Dai). Xiangyang (fell 379) is not inside; the ledger carries it. The page gives no infobox area (only a claimed army of about a million in 383).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 383 shape, holding 383 only: the year of the defeat at Fei River (30 November 383)

keyframe_review.note: 1,277,818 km2 for 383-386, but the pages show the empire breaking up from the end of 383: "Jin forces advanced to the Yellow River and recovered much of the Chinese heartland", Murong Chui rebelled in early 384, Chang'an fell in 385, Lü Guang seized Liang province in 386. The shape (Shandong and Sichuan already gone, Hebei, Shanxi, Hexi still inside) fits 383 only. Years changed to 383; 384 and 385-386 are new keyframes.

correction.text: the 383 shape minus the lands of Later Yan and Later Qin, which left in 384

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "In 384, as Former Qin was recovering from the recent defeat," Murong Chui founded Later Yan, Murong Hong led Western Yan toward Chang'an and Yao Chang founded Later Qin. The shape is the 383 shape without the Later Yan and Later Qin lands that left; the extent of each is Cliopatria's own first shape of those states, the pages give none.

The infobox capitals are Jinyang 385-386 and Nan'an 386-387. Nothing opened gives the land: discs at the two seats are a minimal reading.

The pages contradict it: Chang'an was Later Qin's from 386 ("In 386, Yao Chang occupied the city"); Luoyang was Jin's ("Jin forces" killed Fu Pi in 386 trying to take it; Later Qin took it from Eastern Jin only in 399). The Former Qin infobox places the court at Nan'an (386-387) and Fort Hukong (387-394). The extent of Fu Deng's domain is not on any page opened; the replacement is a minimal reading round the two seats.

ledger.note: 383: Jin wins at Fei River and advances to the Yellow River. 386: Fu Deng is acclaimed emperor at Nan'an after Fu Pi is killed by Jin forces; infobox capital Nan'an 386-387, then Fort Hukong 387-394.

notes: Cliopatria's Former Qin row 353..393 starts two years late (351) and ends a year early (394). Its Wikidata id Q1471995 is shared with the row 'Qin' (-750..-219, the Qin state of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States): they are different states, the id collision is Cliopatria's; this dossier keeps Q1471995. The 387-393 shapes (Chang'an, Luoyang, Kaifeng) are contradicted by the pages and marked wrong; their replacement is a minimal disc reading round the seats the infobox names (Nan'an 386-387, Fort Hukong 387-394), because no page opened gives the extent of Fu Deng's domain. The location of Fort Hukong is not on the page; the Pingliang disc and the capital coordinates for it are the researcher's guess. The 383-386 shape is a single outline over the collapse; replaced by the 383 shape for 383 and new keyframes for 384 and 385-386. The page gives no area figure (infobox or text), so no comparison with Cliopatria's 1.8 M km2 maximum was possible. Not settled for want of pages (budget five): the Tarim and Western Regions in 382-384 (Lü Guang 'conquered Kucha' in 384 per the Later Liang page; the Former Qin page sends him in 382), the date and terms of Former Liang's vassalage to Former Qin (the Former Liang page puts it after the mid-350s), Dai's earlier vassalage, the 'envoys from Silla and Goguryeo' (undated), the lands of Fu Pi in 385-386 beyond Jinyang. Counterparts without a dossier: dai-sixteen-kingdoms (310-376), chouchi (Di state, conquered 371). Predecessors: the page does not say whose land Fu Jiàn took in 351.
